vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: kubernetes
Version: 1.0.5

The bundle is a highly sophisticated and well-documented multi-agent system designed for Kubernetes and OpenShift platform engineering. It establishes a 'swarm' of specialized agents (Jarvis, Atlas, Shield, etc.) with a robust infrastructure for state management, audit logging (LOGS.md), and environment-aware guardrails (SESSION.md). The bundle includes numerous utility scripts for cluster health, security auditing (security-audit.sh, rbac-audit.sh), and automated documentation. While the agents possess high-privilege capabilities necessary for cluster management, the instructions explicitly mandate human-in-the-loop approval for destructive or sensitive operations, and the 'skill-improvement-pr.sh' mechanism for continuous learning is transparently documented and requires human review of generated pull requests.

llm.summary: The skill's code and runtime instructions broadly match a multi-agent Kubernetes platform tool, but there are metadata inconsistencies and a high-risk install/runtime model (downloading and executing many scripts from an external GitHub repo) that merit careful review before use.

dimensions.detail: The skill name/description (platform agent swarm for Kubernetes/OpenShift) matches the included files and scripts: many agent-specific SKILL.md files and dozens of bash helpers for cluster ops, GitOps, security, observability, artifacts, and devex. Requiring kubectl/oc/helm/kustomize/jq/git/curl and a KUBECONFIG is coherent for this purpose. However, the registry metadata shown at the top of the submission claims 'Required env vars: none' and 'Required binaries: none' which contradicts the SKILL.md that explicitly lists required binaries and KUBECONFIG; that metadata mismatch is an important inconsistency to resolve before trusting the package.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and included agent SKILLs explicitly instruct running many bash scripts that perform cluster reads and writes (provisioning namespaces, RBAC, etc.), create logs/memory files, and can perform destructive actions (promote, rollback, cleanup, delete) if enabled. The SKILL.md warns that human approval for production is procedural, not technically enforced, and instructs to audit scripts locally; but the runtime instructions and scripts give broad discretion to change cluster state and write persistent files (logs/WORKING/MEMORY). The scripts expect full cluster access via KUBECONFIG and can call cloud provider APIs when cloud creds are provided. This scope is expected for a cluster-management swarm, but it is powerful and requires strict operational controls (approval gates, least-privilege kubeconfig, restricted token scopes).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The repository is intended to be pulled from a third-party GitHub (https://github.com/kcns008/cluster-agent-swarm-skills) via 'npx skills add' or git clone. There is no registry install spec recorded in the metadata, yet the SKILL.md documents a scripted install that writes/exposes many bash scripts to disk. Downloading and executing unpinned scripts from an external GitHub repo is high risk unless you pin to a verified tag/commit and audit contents. The SKILL.md correctly recommends pinning and auditing, but the default install path (npx with a tree URL or cloning main) can execute arbitrary code from an unknown owner — treat it as untrusted until verified.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires cluster credentials (KUBECONFIG) and optionally cloud/provider/service tokens (AWS/Azure/GCP, ArgoCD, Vault, GitHub) which are proportionate to the features described. Nothing in the instructions asks for unrelated credentials. That said, the top-level registry metadata omitted these requirements — another inconsistency. Also, optional tokens (GitHub, Vault) grant the skill ability to push changes or read secrets if provided; only enable tokens with the minimum scope required and prefer service accounts with restricted, namespace-scoped permissions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill persists state in repository files (logs/LOGS.md, memory/MEMORY.md, incidents/INCIDENTS.md, WORKING.md) and the orchestrator can create PRs (skill-improvement-pr.sh) and write files. Persistence and the ability to commit/create PRs increase blast radius if misused. The skill does not request 'always: true' and does not declare any platform-level auto-enablement, which is appropriate. However, the SKILL.md warns that human-approval is procedural and must be enforced by your platform — do not rely on the agent's self-imposed guardrails alone.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to be a comprehensive, script-heavy Kubernetes/OpenShift multi-agent toolkit — useful but powerful. Before installing: 1) Verify the GitHub source and pin to a specific release tag or commit (do not use main). 2) Locally clone and audit all scripts, especially those with names like delete/cleanup/promote/rollback; search for any network calls, undocumented endpoints, or commands that write credentials to disk. 3) Provide only a least-privilege KUBECONFIG (namespace-scoped service account) and limited cloud/GitHub tokens with minimal scopes; avoid owner/root credentials. 4) Enforce a technical human-approval gate for production operations (block agent from executing destructive commands in prod by policy). 5) Consider running the skill in an isolated non-production sandbox first. 6) Be cautious using 'npx skills add' or any installer that downloads and executes remote scripts — prefer cloning the repo and manually installing vetted artifacts. Finally, resolve the metadata inconsistency (registry lists no requirements while SKILL.md does) with the publisher before trusting automated installs.
